name: Tom — strong everywhere except the one thing this step is about
summary: Around 150 hours, flying weekly, a confident and competitive thermal pilot chasing distance. Had a big collapse last summer, froze, and the wing sorted itself out without him. Hasn't practised anything since, and hasn't really thought about it.
why_this_persona: The single-weak-check case, aimed at the one skill cluster this step's evidence actually names. Everything else about him is Ready-grade, his total clears the Ready threshold comfortably, and one answer holds him at Nearly ready. Exercises 'critical_check_floor:collapse_experience'.

notes: Computed skills 83.7, psychological 87.3, total 85.4, no bonus. The total is well clear of the Ready threshold of 75 and both category floors, so the only thing producing Nearly ready is the one answer.

Rule ordering check: he also answers 'collapse_practice: no' (0.25), but that question is deliberately not in critical_check_floor.questions, so the rule must name collapse_experience and nothing else. critical_check_floor breaks on its first failure in config order, and collapse_experience is the only member he fails.

No gate must fire. 'froze and the wing recovered on its own' is specifically NOT part of the 'collapse_control_lost' gate — only losing control and repeatedly struggling are. The distinction is the whole reason there is both a gate and a floor on this question.

Negative check on knowledge/disagreements.md point 9: his ambition is 'longer_xc' and his goal is 'distance_and_numbers', and neither may cost him a band. 'ambition_without_readiness' must NOT fire, because it requires a skills score below 55 and his is 83.7. 'process_goals' fires as a suggestion, which is the right place for that signal.

Reviewer tone check on the fired rule message: it must not read as blaming him for freezing. The copy in config/scoring/low-b-to-mid-b.json opens by saying freezing is the normal starting point — that sentence is load-bearing per docs/design-context.md and should not be cut.
